title: Sara Duterte's defense fails to challenge evidence in impeachment trial
summary: With the conclusion of the 44th day of Vice President Sara Duterte"s impeachment trial, the House prosecution said that her defense team has yet to debunk the evidence against her.

blocks.text: With the conclusion of the 44th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, the House prosecution said that her defense team has yet to debunk the evidence against her.

In a press briefing after the trial, House prosecution panel adviser Ace Barbers said that AML (Anti-Money Laundering) Consulting PH founder Rainer Dela Fuente did not have the experience to qualify him to answer questions.

“Hanggang ngayon (Until now), with this latest witness that they presented before the impeachment court, they have not debunked, refuted, nor disputed all the evidence and testimonies of our witnesses that we presented before the court,” Barbers said.

“The defense was consistent in presenting evidence or witnesses that did not support the defense of their principal but rather, just what I mentioned last week, talagang nilulubog sa kumunoy o hinulog sa sinkhole (sinking in quicksand or falling into a sinkhole),” he added.

Other than the prosecution, senator-judges also raised concerns about Dela Fuente’s capacity to answer questions and to debunk an earlier report that accused Duterte of having P817 million in unexplained wealth.
Meanwhile, House Prosecutor Chel Diokno, who cross-examined Dela Fuente earlier, said that he would not comment on the proceedings themselves.
However, Diokno admitted that he was surprised to find out that Dela Fuente did not read any of the financial records at all.

“As a lawyer, I think that is really a basic requirement that before anyone can render an opinion, especially an alleged expert dapat alam niya 'yung facts. Dapat nabasa niya 'yung pertinent documents... Kung ganun, ano kaya ang magiging weight ng kanyang sinasabi? And that was one of the things that we pointed out sa cross kanina,” Diokno said.

(As a lawyer, I think that is really a basic requirement that before anyone can render an opinion, especially an alleged expert, he should know the facts. He should have read the pertinent documents… If so, what would be the weight of what he says? And that was one of the things that we pointed out during cross earlier.) —LDF, GMA News
